I have a 8.4 CGPA, I did everything 'right', but the thought of spending my next forty years debugging code in a cubicle makes me want to throw up. I don't even know what I want anymore—every time I try to choose a track, my mind just goes completely blank with dread.

Everyone in my batch is filling out the placements registration form like it's just another daily routine, but I can't even get past the first page. I've switched my interest from web dev to product management, and now to UX design, and I'm just incredibly mediocre at all of them. I feel like a fraud who's just jumping from one trend to another because I'm terrified of committing to a career path and realizing I hate it when it's too late.

If I take this, I'm locked into a 2-year bond doing legacy Java migration, but if I reject it, my placement cell will blacklist me and I'll end up with nothing. I feel trapped in this golden cage before my life has even started, and my chest feels so tight I can barely swallow my food.

I’ve spent four years pulling all-nighters, maintaining a 9.2 CGPA, and for what? To give up the one thing I actually cared about just to become another cog in a corporate machine? I feel so hollow and disillusioned, I don't even want to go to my graduation ceremony next month.

Scrolling through LinkedIn makes me want to throw my phone against the wall. Everyone is posting about their summer internships at FAANG, and my mom keeps asking why I haven't landed anything yet when 'Sharma ji's son' already got a pre-placement offer. I don't even know if I want to do software engineering, but because I took CS, I feel forced to run this race. I'm so paralyzed by the fear of making the wrong choice that I do nothing, and then I hate myself for wasting time.

Everyone is grinding LeetCode and posting their internship offers on LinkedIn, and I'm just sitting here in my room staring at my DSA lab assignment feeling completely frozen. My dad keeps sending me screenshots of my cousin's 25 LPA package, and my chest just tightens up because I don't even know if I want to be a software engineer, but if I don't do this, what else is there?

I chose Mechanical because I actually liked building things, but now all the core jobs pay peanuts and everyone is forcing me to learn web development. I spent the last week struggling with JavaScript while my fluid mechanics midterms are next door, and I just feel this deep, hollow emptiness inside. Why are we running this endless race for a tech job I know I'll hate, just because of some placement stats?

I’m turning twenty-one next week and I have two backlogs in my math courses, no resume to speak of, and absolutely zero direction. I see people in my batch getting placed at top consulting firms and here I am, unable to even decide which elective to take because everything feels like a trap. I feel so small and invisible when my parents talk about the future at the dinner table, like I'm already a failed investment.

I did everything right to get into this tier-1 college, cracked the entrance exams, kept my CGPA above 9, and yet I woke up today feeling completely numb. Is this the prize we sacrificed our entire youth for?

If I don't sit for placements, my dad will think I'm a massive failure, but every time I open LeetCode, my chest gets incredibly tight and I just want to disappear.

Every time I try to talk to my roommates about how lost I feel about our major selection, they just laugh it off and say 'bro, just get a high package first, then do whatever you want.' But I look at the seniors who got those high packages and they look so burnt out and dead inside. I don't want to spend the next ten years of my life chasing something I already know will make me miserable, but the fear of being left behind is making me physically sick.

Everyone in my batch is grinding LeetCode, uploading their certificates on LinkedIn, and talking about 40 LPA packages. I spent the last three hours trying to debug a single DFS function in my DSA lab and just ended up staring at my wall. My dad keeps forwarding me WhatsApp articles about AI taking over coding jobs and asking why I didn't take up Core branches instead. I don't even like coding, but I don't know what else to do. If I step out of this transition, I feel like I'll just fall behind and never catch up. What if I make the wrong choice and end up miserable and broke?

I got my CGPA back today—8.9. On paper, I should be happy, but honestly, I just feel totally numb. I look at these upcoming campus placements and feel this hollow emptiness inside, like I'm preparing to sign my life away to some corporate sweatshop just to make my parents proud. They keep talking about security and comparing me to my cousin who landed an on-campus offer last month. But what is the point of running this endless race when the prize at the finish line is a cubicle that drains your soul? I don't know who I am outside of this academic checklist.

I have two backlogs from last semester, and the placements registration closes next Tuesday. My friends are busy mock-interviewing each other in the hostel rooms, and I'm just sitting here on my bed, unable to even open my laptop. I'm completely paralyzed. Part of me wants to drop out and try something creative, but the dread of failing and having my relatives look at me with pity is literally suffocating. I feel like a massive disappointment waiting to happen, and I'm just watching the train wreck in slow motion.

It's late at night, and I can't sleep because of this constant, tight knot in my chest. I'm in my final year of BTech, and I've realized I absolutely hate engineering, but I've already spent lakhs on fees and four years of my life. My peers are talking about MS in the US or joining consulting firms, and I'm lying here wondering why I didn't have the courage to pursue psychology or design when I had the chance. I feel like I've ruined my life before it even properly started, and there's no way to undo this timeline.

I went to a college fest today and saw all these alumni talking about how they 'found their passion' and built startups, and it made me want to throw up. I don't have a passion. I don't even have a preference; I just feel completely numb to everything, whether it's software, product management, or marketing. I've tried doing different internships, but everything feels like the same tedious, soul-crushing routine. Why does everyone else have this burning spark while I'm just drifting like a ghost through my own youth?

My dad just sent me another screenshot of a tech lead role from some distant cousin's LinkedIn, right when I was staring at my pending DSA assignment. I have a 8.9 CGPA but honestly, every time I open VS Code, my hands feel heavy and my mind just goes completely blank. I don't even want this SDE job, but my parents keep talking about the 'dream package' like my entire life's worth is tied to some placement PPT. What if I make the wrong choice, reject the safe corporate route, and end up a complete failure while everyone else moves ahead?

It's 3 AM and the registration portal for placement season closes tomorrow morning, and I still haven't clicked submit. Everyone's talking about backend dev roles and fintech consulting, and I'm just sitting here crying over my sketchbooks wondering how I got stuck in a mechanical engineering degree. If I register, I commit to a desk job I'll hate for years, but if I walk away to build a design portfolio, I have zero safety net and my backlogs are already making me feel so insecure. I'm completely paralyzed.

I cleared the first two rounds of coding interviews for this massive MNC, and instead of feeling happy, I just felt this deep, hollow numbness in my chest. Everyone on the college WhatsApp group is hyping me up, but I feel like an absolute fraud who is just checking boxes to survive. I don't want to code for the rest of my life, but I also have no clue what else I'd even do—it feels like my brain has been so fried by semester exams that I've lost the ability to actually want things for myself.

I turned twenty-one last week and all I did was stare at my academic transcript feeling this sick feeling in my stomach. My peers are getting research internships abroad and talk passionately about machine learning, while I'm still trying to figure out if I actually like my major or if I just picked it because of the high average package stats. I feel like I'm running a marathon on a track I never chose, and now it's too late to step off because I've already invested three years of tuition.

My mom spent an hour today on the phone talking about my senior who landed a 20 LPA job, and she kept asking when my mock interviews start. I haven't even finished my final year project because my group is barely functional and I just feel so incredibly small and stupid. I want to tell her that I want to take a gap year to just breathe and figure out my interests, but the sheer guilt of being a financial burden while being so clueless is eating me alive.

Everyone in my hostel wing has their life mapped out. They are grinding LeetCode, clearing Amazon rounds, and discussing stock options. Meanwhile, I'm sitting here in my 6th semester with an 8.4 CGPA, completely frozen. I don't even know if I want to write code for the next thirty years of my life, but if I don't register for placements tomorrow, my dad will have a breakdown. He's already comparing me to my cousin who landed a 24 LPA package. I feel like I'm stepping onto a conveyor belt that leads to a soul-crushing void.

I just closed LinkedIn after scrolling for ten minutes and my chest literally hurts. My lab partner just posted about getting into an Ivy League MS program, and two of my school friends just got pre-placement offers. I have three backlogs in mechanical engineering, my parents are asking me what my '5-year plan' is, and I spent the whole day staring at my compiler design notes unable to read a single line. I don't want a 5-year plan. I don't even know how to survive till the end of this semester without losing my mind.

I cleared the tech rounds for a mass recruiter yesterday, and instead of feeling happy, I went to the washroom and cried. It felt like a death sentence. My parents are ecstatic because 'job security' is all they care about, but the thought of spending my 20s writing boilerplate Java in a cubicle makes me feel dead inside. I wanted to try UX design or maybe even write, but everyone says those are unstable hobbies, not real careers. I feel like I'm selling my soul before I've even had a chance to use it.

I'm in my final year of B.Com, and my dad expects me to join his accounting firm, but every single day I walk into class I feel this heavy, hollow dread. My friends are preparing for CAT, some are joining startups, and I'm just drifting. I tried to study for the CA exams but my brain literally shuts down after ten minutes. I feel like a massive disappointment in a family of high-achievers. I don't know what my 'passion' is, and the pressure to find one is paralyzing me from doing anything at all.

I missed my branch change cutoff by 0.1 GPA. Now I'm stuck in Chemical Engineering, a branch I have zero interest in, while all the CS guys are getting hyped up for coding bootcamps. I sit in these fluid mechanics lectures and think, 'Why am I even here?' I try to self-study python at night but I'm so exhausted from lab reports that I just end up staring at the ceiling. I'm terrified that this one stupid GPA score has permanently locked me out of a good life and I'm destined to be mediocre.

I just spent 14 hours straight debugging my DSA assignments and practicing LeetCode because placement season starts in three months, but honestly? I felt absolutely nothing when the test cases finally passed green. My dad sent me a screenshot of some relative's kid landing a 40 LPA package at an MNC, asking if I'm 'on track' for something similar. I looked at my 8.7 CGPA and just wanted to throw up. I don't even know if I want to be a software engineer, but if I don't do this, what else is there? I feel like I'm running at full speed toward a cliff, pretending I actually want to jump.

Everyone in my batch is filling out their preferences for the branch electives and core pathways, and they all seem so sure of themselves. Some want system design, some are preping for civil services, and I'm just sitting here staring at the registration portal with my hands shaking. I changed my major once already, and if I pick the wrong specialization now, I feel like I'm locked in forever. My mom keeps saying 'follow your passion' but I don't have one—I just have a collection of half-finished hobbies and an overwhelming fear of being stuck in a cubicle doing something I hate for the next forty years.

My LinkedIn feed is pure poison right now. Every single day it’s 'I am thrilled to announce my internship at...' or 'Grateful to receive the offer from...'. I got rejected in the second round of three different campus placement interviews this week, and honestly, the worst part isn't even the rejection—it's the relief I felt when they said no. But then the panic sets in because my midterms are starting, my project partner is ignoring my texts, and my parents are expecting me to support them in a few years. I feel like an absolute fraud who is failing before the race has even properly started.

I’m in my final semester and I have zero backlogs, a decent CGPA, and a job offer lined up at an IT consultancy. By all standards, I should be celebrating, but instead I spent last night crying on my bathroom floor. The thought of waking up every day at 8 AM to write corporate code for some client I don't care about makes me feel utterly empty inside. My peers tell me to just take the money and be grateful because 'the market is brutal,' but I feel like I'm selling the best years of my life for a steady paycheck and a slow death of my soul.

I had to sit through another family dinner where my uncle spent two hours talking about how his son got into a top-tier business school, and then everyone turned to look at me. I'm a third-year student, my grades are slipping because of burnout, and I can't even decide if I want to prepare for higher studies or sit for placements. I feel like a chameleon trying to blend into whatever expectation is thrown at me next, completely losing track of what I actually like. I don't want to disappoint my family, but trying to live out their blueprint for my life is literally suffocating me.

I just finished my 5th DSA lab of the week, my hands are literally shaking, and my dad just sent a screenshot of some relative's kid getting a 45 LPA package at Atlassian. I look at my 7.8 CGPA and these half-finished LeetCode problems and my chest just feels completely hollow. I don't even want to be a software engineer, but if I don't sit for placements next month, what else is there? I feel like I'm running full speed off a cliff just because everyone else is.

Everyone on my LinkedIn is posting about their summer analyst internships at MBB firms or FAANG, and I’m sitting here during midterms literally unable to choose a single project topic because nothing feels real. I spent the last three years keeping my GPA at 9.2, but now that the actual job portals are opening, I feel this sickening numbness. Is this it? Am I supposed to spend the next forty years of my life optimizing database queries or making PowerPoint decks just to pay rent?

I have two backlogs from last semester, and the placement cell just sent out the registration link for the day-0 companies. I clicked on it and my mind just went blank; I couldn't even fill out my home address without feeling like crying. My roommates are talking about system design interviews and I'm still trying to figure out if I even like coding or if I just did this because my JEE prep center told me it was the only way to survive. I feel so small and so incredibly stuck.

My mom called today asking if I'm preparing for the bank PO exams or the UPSC, since my tech placements aren't looking good. I lied and said yes, but the truth is I can't even get out of bed to go to my morning lectures anymore. I look at the syllabus, the mock test schedules, the corporate job descriptions, and they all look like different cages to me. Why does everyone else seem to fit so easily into these boxes while I feel like I'm suffocating?

I’m in my final year of chemical engineering, but I spent all my free time doing UI/UX design because I actually loved it. But now, with the recession, no design agencies are hiring freshers, and the placement coordinator told me to just apply for core refinery roles or mass IT recruiters. I feel like I’m being forced to bury the only part of myself I actually cared about just to get a salary slip. I feel so betrayed by the system.

I’ve spent the last three days staring at this DSA coding lab, but my brain has completely shut down. My dad keeps sending me screenshots of my cousin’s 24 LPA package from some fintech firm, asking me what my 'plan' is for the placements next month. The truth is, I don’t even know if I want to write code for the rest of my life, but I've spent four years and so much of my parents' money on this degree. I feel like I'm standing at a massive crossroads with a blindfold on, and choosing any path feels like I'm setting myself up for a life of quiet misery.

Every time I open LinkedIn, it’s just a barrage of 'I’m thrilled to announce...' and people getting these massive summer internships. I sit there with my 8.2 CGPA and a blank resume, feeling absolutely hollowed out. I keep shifting from 'maybe I should prep for UPSC' to 'let me just grind LeetCode' to 'maybe I'll do an MBA,' but I don't actually care about any of them. I'm just running because everyone else is, but my legs are giving out and I honestly don't see the point of the finish line.

I chose Mechanical because I actually liked making things, but now that placement season is here, all the core companies are offering peanuts compared to the IT roles. My friends are telling me to just do a 3-month boot camp and pivot to web development, but the thought of sitting in a cubicle debugging JavaScript makes me want to scream. I feel so trapped between wanting financial stability to help my family and wanting to do something that doesn't slowly kill my soul.

I have two active backlogs from my fifth semester and my grades are a joke. While my batchmates are discussing which product-based companies are visiting campus, I'm literally just praying some mass recruiter will pick me up so I don't end up jobless at graduation. But even if they do, I look at the future and just feel this cold, numb terror. Is this it? Am I just destined to be a low-paid cog in some MNC because I couldn't handle college physics?

I got a 9.1 on my midterms and everyone tells me I have a bright future, but I feel completely empty inside. I've spent years checking every single academic box, doing every assignment perfectly, but now that I have to choose a career path, I realize I don't have a single genuine interest of my own. I've spent so long being the 'good student' that I don't even know who I am when I'm not studying for an exam. I'm terrified of making the wrong choice and realizing I wasted my entire life living someone else's script.
